title: Finite-prefix division of high-length monoid series
statement:
Let $G\cong\mathbf Z^r$ be a free abelian group of finite rank, $P\subseteq G$ an additive submonoid generated by nonzero $g_1,\ldots,g_s$, and $w:G	o\mathbf Z$ a group homomorphism strictly positive on $P\setminus\{0\}$. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and equip $B=A^P$ with componentwise addition and finite convolution as in [lem-trf-positive-monoid-convolution-length], and write $z^p\in B$ for the family with coefficient $1$ at $p$ and $0$ elsewhere. Let $
u(p)$ be the maximum number of nonzero summands of $p$, with $
u(0)=0$, and fix $n\ge1$. Put $H_n=\{p:
u(p)\ge n\}$, $T=\{1,\ldots,s\}^n$ with any fixed total order, and $s_I=\sum_{j=1}^n g_{i_j}$ for $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_n)$. Every $p\in H_n$ has $p=s_I+q$ for some $I\in T$ and $q\in P$. Define $E_I$ to consist of those $p\in H_n$ for which $I$ is the first tuple with $p-s_I\in P$, subtraction taken in $G$. The $E_I$ are pairwise disjoint and have union $H_n$. For every family $a\in A^P$, let $a^{\ge n}_p=a_p$ on $H_n$ and zero elsewhere, and define $c^I_q=a_{s_I+q}$ if $s_I+q\in E_I$, and $c^I_q=0$ otherwise. Then $z^{s_I}c^I$ equals $a$ on $E_I$ and zero off $E_I$, and $a^{\ge n}=\sum_{I\in T}z^{s_I}c^I$. This is a finite sum of elements of $B$, and $z^{s_I}=z^{g_{i_1}}\cdots z^{g_{i_n}}$. If $s=0$, then $P=\{0\}$, $H_n=T=\varnothing$, and this identity is the empty-sum identity. No convergence or support restriction is imposed on the families $c^I$.

proof.text: Since the $g_i$ generate $P$, write each $h_j$ as a finite sum of generators. Each list is nonempty because its sum is nonzero. Concatenate these lists to obtain $p=g_{k_1}+\cdots+g_{k_L}$ with $L\ge m\ge n$. Take $I=(k_1,\ldots,k_n)$ and let $q$ be the sum of the remaining generators, or $0$ if $L=n$. Then $q\in P$ and $p=s_I+q$, proving coverage.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, formal monoid models; agent-supplied auxiliary coefficient argument, old steps 6--7: coverage by generator prefixes, first-eligible partition, residual coefficient families and their finite shifted-sum identity. Not asserted to be a theorem stated in ILO. Proof step 2.

proof.text: The set $T$ has $s^n$ elements. For each $p\in H_n$, step 2 makes $\{I\in T:p-s_I\in P\}$ nonempty. A nonempty finite totally ordered set has a unique least element (successively keep the smaller element in a finite enumeration). Consequently $p$ lies in exactly one $E_I$. By definition no $E_I$ contains a point outside $H_n$, proving disjointness and the asserted union.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, formal monoid models; agent-supplied auxiliary coefficient argument, old steps 6--7: coverage by generator prefixes, first-eligible partition, residual coefficient families and their finite shifted-sum identity. Not asserted to be a theorem stated in ILO. Proof step 3.

proof.text: Each displayed rule for $c^I$ gives one element of $A$ for every $q\in P$, hence an element of $B=A^P$. Apply the shift formula of [lem-trf-positive-monoid-convolution-length] with $s_0=s_I$. At $p=s_I+q$ the product coefficient is $c^I_q$, hence $a_p$ if $p\in E_I$ and $0$ otherwise. If no such $q$ exists the product coefficient is $0$, and $p\notin E_I$ by eligibility. Uniqueness of $q$ is cancellation in $G$. This proves the claimed coefficient formula everywhere.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, formal monoid models; agent-supplied auxiliary coefficient argument, old steps 6--7: coverage by generator prefixes, first-eligible partition, residual coefficient families and their finite shifted-sum identity. Not asserted to be a theorem stated in ILO. Proof step 4.

proof.text: Addition in $B$ is componentwise by [lem-trf-positive-monoid-convolution-length]. For $p\in H_n$, exactly one summand in the finite sum over $T$ has coefficient $a_p$ by steps 3--4, and all other coefficients are $0$. For $p\notin H_n$ all summands have coefficient $0$. Thus the sum has precisely the coefficients of $a^{\ge n}$, and equality follows as equality of functions on $P$. Only a finite sum over $T$ occurs; the $c^I$ need neither finite support nor convergence.

Not asserted to be a theorem stated in ILO. Proof step 5.

proof.text: The monomial identity $z^uz^v=z^{u+v}$ of [lem-trf-positive-monoid-convolution-length] proves $\prod_{j=1}^n z^{g_{i_j}}=z^{s_I}$ by induction on $n$: for $n=1$ it is the same monomial, and adjoining the last factor adds $g_{i_n}$ to the exponent.

source.place: Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, formal monoid models; agent-supplied auxiliary coefficient argument, old steps 6--7: coverage by generator prefixes, first-eligible partition, residual coefficient families and their finite shifted-sum identity. Not asserted to be a theorem stated in ILO. Proof step 6.

proof.text: If $s=0$, generation means $P=\{0\}$. Since $\nu(0)=0$ and $n\ge1$, $H_n=\varnothing$; also there is no length-$n$ tuple in the empty alphabet, so $T=\varnothing$. Hence $a^{\ge n}=0$ and the sum is the empty sum $0$. The partition and individual product assertions are vacuous.
